title: Sign up and sign in with email + OTP only
steps: 1. Open the app and tap Sign up. 2. Enter name, a real @thapar.edu email and roll number. 3. Tap Send code. 4. Open the email and type the 6-digit code into the app.
expected: A code email arrives within a minute. Entering it signs you in. No password is asked for at any point.

title: Non-college email is refused in the app before any code is sent
steps: 1. On the sign-up screen enter someone@gmail.com. 2. Tap Send code.
expected: The app shows an error asking for a @thapar.edu address. No email is sent.

title: Roll number already registered
steps: 1. Sign up with a roll number already used by another account. 2. Enter the OTP.
expected: The app says the roll number is already registered, keeps you on the screen with the roll number editable, and lets you correct it with 'Save roll number & continue'.

title: Upload ID card from camera or gallery
steps: 1. After signing up, open the ID card screen. 2. Take a photo of the student ID card (or pick one from the gallery). 3. Submit.
expected: The upload succeeds and the profile shows 'Verification pending'.

title: Sign out
steps: 1. Profile tab → Sign out. 2. Try to open Chats.
expected: You are returned to the guest feed; Chats asks you to sign in.

title: Stay signed in after closing the app
steps: 1. Sign in. 2. Swipe the app away (force close). 3. Open it again.
expected: You are still signed in and land on the feed.

title: Guest is asked to sign in for anything except browsing
steps: 1. Open the app without signing in. 2. Open a listing and tap Chat with seller. 3. Tap the + (List) tab.
expected: Each action shows a sign-in prompt instead of doing the action. The listing shows 'Sign in to see the meeting point'.

title: Nearest-first feed after choosing a hostel
steps: 1. Profile → Your hostel → pick Agira Hall. 2. Home → switch to Nearest.
expected: Listings meeting at Agira Hall come first, each card shows a distance. Changing the hostel re-sorts the feed.

title: Meeting point chosen from a searchable campus list
steps: 1. + tab → create a listing. 2. Tap Meeting point and type 'lib'.
expected: A searchable list of campus places appears and filters to Library. Free text cannot be saved.

title: Messages and offers in one timeline
steps: 1. Open a chat. 2. Send a message, then make an offer, then send another message.
expected: The three appear in the order they were sent, the offer as a card with Accept / Reject for the other person.

title: Messages arrive live
steps: 1. Open the same chat on two phones (buyer and seller). 2. Send a message from one.
expected: It appears on the other phone within about 5 seconds without refreshing (NFR-PRF-5).

title: Scan the QR with the phone camera at the meetup
steps: 1. Seller: open the paid deal, add a condition photo, tap Show QR. 2. Buyer: open the deal, add a condition photo, tap Scan QR and point the camera at the seller's screen.
expected: The scan is accepted, both phones show 'Completed' and the money is released to the seller.

title: Deal status is clear to both sides
steps: 1. Follow one sale from 'Waiting for payment' to 'Completed' on both phones.
expected: Each step shows a plain-language status and the next action for the person viewing (NFR-USE-2).

title: Push notification on a phone (needs a development build)
steps: 1. Install the development build (not Expo Go). 2. Sign in and allow notifications. 3. From another account, send this user an offer. 4. Lock the phone.
expected: A notification 'New offer …' appears on the lock screen; tapping it opens the chat.

title: Review tab only for admins
steps: 1. Sign in as a student and look at the tab bar. 2. Sign in as an admin (users.role = admin).
expected: Students have no Review tab. The admin sees Review with Dashboard, Listings, IDs and Disputes.

title: Admin dashboard in a web browser
steps: 1. Run the app for web (npx expo start --web). 2. Sign in as an admin in the browser. 3. Open Review → Dashboard.
expected: The dashboard shows clearance time against the 4-hour target, the deal metrics and platform totals, and the queues work in the browser.
